prerequisites: Materials Science and Engineering: metallic materials
Technical drawing representation and reading and CAD/CAM technologies
Background on statics, kinematics, stress and strain states and constitutive laws of materials

learning_outcomes.text: General principles of conventional subtractive manufacturing processes and manufacturing processes based on metal forming technologies.
To know the technologies associated with each process (machines, tools, operations, applications).
Select the most efficient manufacturing processes, taking into account the specifications of the products.
To establish the best sequence of production steps for different products.
Application of CAD / CAM systems in the definition of machining strategies.
Contact with machining technologies (use of CNC equipment, demonstrations, and machinability tests).
Characterization of plastic and fracture behaviour of materials by testing.

syllabus_topics: Conventional Machining Processes (Turning, Drilling, Reaming, Milling, Grinding)
CNC machining: lathes, milling machines and machining centres
assessment_rules: The final mark (FM) is calculated as A*0.80 + B*0.20, where A is the average grade on the two quizzes (partial tests) and B is the group assignment grade. Students must achieve a minimum weighted average of 10 points and a minimum grade of 7.0 points in each evaluation test (quizzes). Eligibility for exams requires at least 75% attendance in practical classes and successful completion of the group assignment with a score of at least 10 points. Students not meeting approval requirements may access a global resource exam (80% weight) or partial resource exams (40% weight each). Approved students may access a resource exam for grade improvement.
